plan: With a private value of $9, I want to maximize potential profit. In Stage 2's descending clock mechanism, I'll aim to claim the item just above my value. Since my value is $9, I'll bid strategically to win if the clock drops to near my value. A bid around $9.50 seems optimal - high enough to potentially win, but not so high that I lose money if I acquire the item. This balances winning probability with profit margin.

My private value is $20. In Stage 2's descending clock auction, I want to claim the item when the price reaches my sealed bid. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly below my value. If I bid too high, I risk paying more than the item's worth. If I bid too low, I might miss winning. A bid around $19-$19.5 seems optimal - close to my value but with a small profit margin.

In a single-round sealed bid auction with a descending clock, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically based on my private value of $20. I want to maximize my potential profit. Since the first to claim at their bid wins, I'll bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning while ensuring I only win if the price is favorable. A bid around $21-$22 seems reasonable to balance winning probability and potential profit margin.
